# MoGe3 authentic references

The reference source is the unchanged MoGe3 and shared DINOv2/interpolation implementation from `Blaizzy/mlx-vlm` revision `abd3b2d7b728cb5372d4e092260da325e5ded209`. `upstream_loader.py` registers package paths and executes the original `BaseModelConfig` class AST to avoid unrelated language-model imports; it does not replace model mathematics. Download/extract that revision and pass its root as `--source`.

`checkpoints.json` records pinned Hugging Face revisions and SHA-256 hashes for both complete published checkpoints. Header inspection found 607 F32 tensors for ViT-L and 831 F32 tensors for ViT-g. These are storage observations; each full reference run separately records every loaded parameter dtype and input/output dtype.

## Small CPU oracles

```bash
python generate_small_oracles.py --source /path/to/mlx-vlm --output /path/to/output
```

Requires MLX and NumPy. The generator explicitly selects CPU. The six-voxel fixture includes adjacent and isolated voxels in a `(1,5,5,5)` extent, all 27 neighbors, three output channels, ceil-div pooling coordinates/parent indices and nearest upsampling. The geometry fixture uses a sloped plane with known focal 1.7; upstream recovers 1.700005054473877 (absolute error below 1e-4). It includes fixed-focal and empty-mask paths, plus a nonzero 0.35 depth shift recovered as 0.3500001132488251 to exercise optimizer updates. Searchsorted fixtures cover duplicate values, both sides, empty sorted input and signed int64 values beyond float32 exact representation.

Generated with exact MLX 0.32.5 on CPU; the sparse fixture and initial geometry cases regenerated byte-identically; the final geometry fixture additionally includes the verified nonzero-shift case:

- `sparse-oracle.json`: `43ad8501ef281c4114d1b9d6a6f3cb8322e74540a6b0141898b4af9cb70d8e0e`
- `geometry-search-oracle.json`: `233ca2e3d1c47cf40e36f711bcf5a8cd6deca870e38a6964deac0664ee516301`

## Full real-model reference

```bash
MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 python generate_reference.py \
  --source /path/to/mlx-vlm \
  --model /path/to/moge-3-vitl-mlx-fp32 \
  --image ../sam3/cats.png --device gpu \
  --opts '{"resolution_level":9,"refine_steps":3,"return_per_step":true}' \
  --output /path/to/reference.safetensors
```

Requires MLX, NumPy and Pillow. Repeat with the giant checkpoint; use `--device cpu` for CPU comparisons. `provenance.json` is mandatory: the harness checks every pinned source module before importing model code, the loaded binding and mapped native-library hashes/version, and checkpoint/config/preprocessor/image hashes before loading weights. Missing or mismatched identities fail even under `python -O`. TF32 must be disabled before starting the process. The generator strictly loads all checkpoint keys, retains F32 weights, saves every output (including all requested refinement steps), and writes a sibling JSON with options, hashes, dtypes, shapes, finite counts and mapped native libraries. Per-step lists become `points_stepN`, `depth_stepN` and `intrinsics_stepN` only in serialization.

The fixed image reuses the existing lossless `../sam3/cats.png`; no decoder-dependent JPEG conversion is involved. Resolution level 9 always selects 3600 base tokens, independently of image output dimensions. Invalid masked depth/points retain upstream positive infinity; invalid normals are zero. Compare exact keys/shapes, mask and finite support before relative RMS. GPU depth/points tolerance is 5e-3 with TF32 disabled; CPU tolerance is 1e-4; intrinsics tolerance is 1e-3.

The Linux validation runtime uses MLX native pin `bff10220c742907f0c68e55ff174aaea56f74e3d`, with library SHA-256 `9e38e9292550ea8eec9eb1877d06b72f5155ff382ac0e4ec1054818e15276094` and binding SHA-256 `f8ec0f363bc6eab1cda644a2579ae43aa663939f30ace531d5fb8cc33c7090cc`. Its isolated binding was rebuilt from exact headers; copied ELF visibility changes preserve every native executable section. Runtime reconstruction/provenance is retained in `.cache/epic-2382/python-exact-core`; no user Python environment is modified.

Authentic full GPU references completed for ViT-L and ViT-g at resolution9/refine3 with all17 outputs. Their tensor SHA-256 values are respectively `8a52dfd2f1d4f6fa7e9e955fd4ab3366bf4cb66c9de1b19816306c6917280a61` and `b3a52681524456798639eef2971422edbd6113ea7b6188bb7b019bcd25b09cd7`. Source/runtime/checkpoint/image hashes and option-derived schemas were independently reverified after harness hardening, preserving original receipts and tensors. The sequential authenticated Rust GPU comparison passed all five cases: maximum depth/points relative RMS was 2.2250e-5/2.0331e-5 (limit 5e-3), and maximum intrinsics absolute error was 2.0802e-5 (limit 1e-3). Exact mask and finite/NaN/infinity support checks passed. CPU parity remains pending the original full-resolution CPU reference; GPU evidence does not substitute for that gate.

Compare serialized outputs with:

```bash
python compare_reference.py actual.safetensors reference.safetensors --device gpu --report comparison.json
```

The comparator requires all five standard outputs and identical complete key sets, including refinement steps. It rejects shape, mask, finite-support, NaN or infinity-sign differences before computing metrics; empty finite support is not a pass. Intrinsics use maximum absolute error, and other floating outputs use relative RMS on the shared finite support.

The comparator requires an actual `.json` receipt beside the Rust artifact with `implementation: "rust"`, build `revision`, actual `output_sha256`, pinned `checkpoint_sha256` and `image_sha256`, `image_shape`, exact `options`, actual `device`, and `tf32: "0"`. The reference receipt additionally requires pinned source hashes/revision and a verified native/binding runtime receipt. A `.verified.json` reference receipt takes precedence when retained historical outputs were independently verified. The comparator rejects mismatched options/checkpoint/backend rather than trusting its tolerance selector. `return_per_step` requires exactly contiguous step0 through step`refine_steps` for points/depth/intrinsics with matching shapes.

The GPU cases in `full-reference-manifest.json` use these exact option overrides (all unspecified options retain the normalized defaults). Pass each JSON object to `--opts` in the command above; the manifest records the complete normalized options and all output hashes/shapes.

| Case | Checkpoint | Options | Output keys |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `vitl-gpu-resolution9` | ViT-L | `{"resolution_level":9,"refine_steps":3,"return_per_step":true}` | 17 |
| `vitg-gpu-resolution9` | ViT-g | `{"resolution_level":9,"refine_steps":3,"return_per_step":true}` | 17 |
| `vitl-no-refine` | ViT-L | `{"resolution_level":9,"refine_steps":0,"force_projection":false,"apply_mask":true}` | 5 |
| `vitl-fixed-unmasked` | ViT-L | `{"resolution_level":9,"refine_steps":3,"return_per_step":true,"fov_x":60,"force_projection":false,"apply_mask":false}` | 17 |
| `vitl-fixed-projected` | ViT-L | `{"resolution_level":0,"num_tokens":3600,"refine_steps":0,"fov_x":60,"force_projection":true,"apply_mask":false}` | 5 |

The last case verifies that an explicit token count takes precedence over the resolution level. On this fixed image the predicted mask is entirely true; this does not imply universal finite outputs. Refinement is nontrivial: step0-to-step3 depth RMS is 0.0059396653 for ViT-L and 0.0042166873 for ViT-g.


The `vitl-default` reference uses no option overrides and contains exactly five tensors. Its SHA-256 is `97cbe3c12ca8553f7f177bc189193f8b29ace8d536a25ab8417d7851d74c31e4`.

Validate the actual CLI with a fresh output directory:

```bash
MLX_ENABLE_TF32=0 python validate_cli.py \
  --binary /path/to/mlxcel --model /path/to/moge-3-vitl-mlx-fp32 \
  --image ../sam3/cats.png --reference /path/to/vitl-default.safetensors \
  --output /path/to/new-cli-output --revision COMMIT --device gpu
```

This driver executes `predict` without `--opts` for the default case. It requires a successful process exit and exactly one recognized `Runtime device:` log entry matching the reference backend before writing the actual receipt or comparing tensors. GPU-to-CPU fallback is rejected. It checks the complete five-tensor schema, depth/normal/mask preview dimensions, camera intrinsics metadata against the stored tensor, and the actual `arch` catalog output. The retained command, binary hash, process log/exit, receipt and validation report attest the invocation; requested environment settings alone do not attest the device.
